implementation_notes: moka is the ecosystem cache for this: get_with(key, |k| load(k)) initializes and inserts atomically on a miss (try_get_with for fallible loaders), time_to_live/time_to_idle and max_capacity carry the expiry and eviction policy, and invalidate(&key) is the write-path step. The cache is thread-safe without an outer lock and cheap to clone across threads, but get returns a clone of the value, so expensive payloads belong behind an Arc; moka::future::Cache is the async form that awaits the loader without blocking a runtime thread.
pitfalls: get() clones the value on every hit (documented behaviour), so store Arc<T> rather than large structures or each read pays a deep copy.
Never wrap the cache in a Mutex or RwLock: it is already thread-safe and the surrounding lock destroys the concurrency it provides.
Eviction and expiry are best-effort: an entry can disappear at any time, so the read path must always be able to reload from the source of truth.

variants.name: Mutex<HashMap> with the entry API (std only)
variants.idiom_name: std::sync::Mutex<HashMap<K, Entry>> with a deadline per entry
variants.implementation_notes: With no dependencies the store is a std::sync::Mutex<HashMap<K, Entry>> (or RwLock for read-heavy maps) and the populate step checks the deadline and inserts under one guard; the guard must be released before the source-of-truth call, because holding a std lock across I/O serializes every reader. In async code a std::sync::Mutex guard cannot be held across an .await, so either the critical section is purely synchronous or the map uses tokio::sync::Mutex. TTL, eviction and invalidation are all application code in this form.
pitfalls: A std::sync::Mutex guard held across an .await does not compile (or deadlocks when two tasks share the lock): scope the guard or use an async mutex.
Mutex poisoning: if a loader panics while holding the lock, later .lock() calls return Err - decide whether to recover the guard or propagate the panic.
A HashMap cache has no capacity bound and leaks until the process runs out of memory unless a sweep task and an eviction rule are added.
